title: Cloud-Native Logging Architecture, Vector Aggregation & Grafana Loki LogQL
summary: Master scalable cloud-native logging: building low-latency log pipelines using Vector / Fluent Bit, high-throughput log aggregation with Grafana Loki, PII redaction and structured JSON parsing, and executing advanced stream and line filter LogQL queries.
learningObjectives: Configure high-throughput log shipping and aggregation using Vector / Fluent Bit DaemonSets with multiline parsing.
Implement privacy compliance and security filters in Vector pipelines to redact sensitive PII (credit cards, tokens) before storage.
Formulate Grafana Loki LogQL queries using stream selectors, line filters (|=, !~), and JSON line unwrapping (| json).

curriculumModules.title: Log Pipeline Architecture, Vector Shipping & PII Redaction
curriculumModules.conceptSummary: Modern cloud-native logging separates collection (node-level DaemonSets scraping /var/log/pods), transformation (Vector/FluentBit parsing JSON, adding Kubernetes metadata, and scrubbing PII), and long-term storage (Grafana Loki or Object Storage). Unindexed, label-only indexing in Loki avoids memory-heavy inverted indexes like Elasticsearch.
curriculumModules.productionArchitecturePattern: Deploy Vector agents on each node to scrub JWT tokens and credit card numbers via regex transforms before shipping compressed streams to Loki, fulfilling GDPR and PCI-DSS compliance.

curriculumModules.title: Grafana Loki Stream Indexing & Advanced LogQL Analysis
curriculumModules.conceptSummary: Grafana Loki indexes metadata labels (e.g. {app='payment', env='prod'}) rather than full log text. LogQL extends this with line filters (|= 'error', != 'timeout'), pattern parsers (| json, | logfmt), and metric queries (rate({app='payment'} |= '500'[5m])). This enables rapid troubleshooting without prohibitive indexing storage costs.
curriculumModules.productionArchitecturePattern: Keep Loki stream label cardinality low ({app, namespace, environment}); use LogQL | json or | pattern during queries to extract dynamic fields (userId, status, latencyMs) on-the-fly.

labs.title: Configuring Vector Log Pipelines with Automated PII Redaction
labs.scenario: Implement automated PII scrubbing in log collection: author a Vector configuration in /logging/vector.yaml defining a kubernetes_logs source, a remap transform redacting credit card numbers with [REDACTED_CC], and a loki sink. Apply this configuration as ConfigMap vector-config in namespace logging.
labs.productionContext: Automated inline PII redaction ensures application logs can be analyzed by engineers without violating security policies or exposing customer payment credentials.
objectives: Author Vector pipeline with remap transform in /logging/vector.yaml.
Deploy ConfigMap vector-config in namespace logging.
labs.starterManifest:
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: vector-config
  namespace: logging
data:
  vector.yaml: |
    sources:
      k8s_logs:
        type: kubernetes_logs
    transforms:
      redact_pii:
        type: remap
        inputs: [k8s_logs]
        source: .message = replace(.message, r'[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{4}', "[REDACTED_CC]")
    sinks:
      loki:
        type: loki
        inputs: [redact_pii]
        endpoint: "http://loki.logging.svc:3100"

assessmentQuestions.question: What is the key architectural difference between Grafana Loki and traditional log indexing systems like Elasticsearch?
options: Loki compresses all logs into zip archives on local hard drives.

Loki only indexes metadata labels for log streams (e.g. {app='web', env='prod'}) rather than the full-text log payload, drastically reducing memory usage, storage costs, and index maintenance overhead while querying payloads on-demand with LogQL.
Loki requires application code to be written exclusively in Golang.
Loki only stores logs for 5 minutes before discarding them.
assessmentQuestions.explanation: By indexing only labels rather than building an inverted index of every word, Loki requires orders of magnitude less memory and storage than Elasticsearch, making it economical to retain petabytes of logs in object storage.

assessmentQuestions.question: In a LogQL query, what is the purpose of the '| json' pipeline stage?
options: It converts the entire server response to HTML.
It parses structured JSON log lines at query time, extracting JSON properties into temporary labels that can be filtered, formatted, or aggregated in subsequent pipeline stages.
It encrypts the log payload using AES-256.
It forces the query to fail if any log line contains numbers.
assessmentQuestions.explanation: The '| json' parser extracts fields from JSON log entries into labels, allowing users to query against dynamic fields (e.g. | status >= 500) without having indexed those fields upfront.
